newsitem.title: USA: Court bars US prosecution of pro-marijuana doctors.
newsitem.headline: Court bars US prosecution of pro-marijuana doctors.

text.p: A judge issued a temporary restraining order on Friday blocking the federal government from prosecuting doctors who recommend marijuana to their patients.
U.S. District Judge Fern Smith of San Francisco also ordered the government to settle through negotiation its dispute with a group of doctors and patients who advocate marijuana for medical use.

Graham Boyd, lead attorney for the doctors and patients who sued the government over the issue, said the restraining order was a major victory. "The court declared a cease-fire in the federal government's war on doctors," Boyd told reporters.

Patricia Seitz, director of the office of legal counsel for the White House Office of National Drug Control Policy, said she was "mildly disappointed" by the temporary order, but said she welcomed negotiations.

At issue is California's Proposition 215, approved by voters last November, which makes it legal under state law for sick people to grow and possess marijuana for medical use when recommended by a doctor. Supporters of the measure say marijuana can help ease the pain of AIDS, cancer, glaucoma and other serious illnesses.
The Clinton administration maintains that marijuana is illegal under federal law and has pledged to punish doctors who recommend its use.

A group of California doctors, patients, medical associations and the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) sued, seeking a court order blocking the federal government from acting against doctors who recommend marijuana.

Supporters of the measure said the government's threat to prosecute doctors discouraged them from talking to their patients about the possible benefits of marijuana and violated their First Amendment free speech rights.

Attorneys for the government told the court that the government's stance did not prevent doctors from discussing the benefits and possible risks of marijuana, only from recommending or prescribing it.

Smith ordered the two sides to define the terms clearly through negotiations. She issued the temporary restraining order after an attorney for the government said it would not hold off prosecuting doctors during negotiations, as the judge had requested.
